page: Microsoft Azure L8s_v4 is an Lsv4-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2168.0 and a strong gzip compression rate of 31.37 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8333.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7995.24. Memory bandwidth is measured at 621.16 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 65.68 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, text generation is strong at 270.03 tokens/sec, though text generation performance drops to a weak 8.36 tokens/sec when scaling to a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L8s_v4 offers high resource density by combining a substantial 1920 GB local NVMe SSD with 64.0 GB of RAM on an 8-vCPU footprint. This makes it highly suitable for storage-intensive and database workloads, such as relational databases, NoSQL stores, and transactional systems that require low-latency local storage. However, a key tradeoff is the weak text generation performance on larger models, indicating that it is not optimized for heavy LLM inference tasks despite the presence of Intel AMX instructions. It is best utilized for database operations, data caching, and general-purpose workloads requiring fast local storage.
